objective: Derive the full pentagon boundary relation, prove the exact three-pin extension theorem, exhibit a minimum four-pin obstruction invisible to all three-terminal projections, and characterize independent exterior-label boundaries and controlled ears.

atomic_claims.text: Every indexed pentagon map is a translation and a permutation of the five generator steps; 120 intersections give the exact boundary relation and counts.
The two-terminal completion counts are (0,312,144) at separation one and (240,144,204) at separation two, for target pair types 0,1,2.
At most three prescribed exterior labels extend precisely when consecutive pinned labels differ.
Four is the minimum pin arity of a pair-compatible but infeasible pentagon boundary; the displayed four-pin witness has every three-pin projection feasible.
When distinct exterior labels are pairwise nonadjacent in B, the full boundary extends exactly when consecutive labels differ.
A fresh complementary pentagon ear extends a given map exactly when the old path has distinct generator colors, with factorially many extensions.

assumptions: Finite simple graph, indexed five-cycle and an actual map of its exterior.
Exterior vertices and labels may repeat, and the exact cyclic positions are retained.
The independent-boundary subtheorem has an explicit target-side nonadjacency hypothesis.
risks: All counts and finite classifications are paper derivations, not executed enumeration.
A prescribed boundary failure is not graph-level nonexistence.
No universal pentagon-ear decomposition or universal independent boundary is asserted.
Three-terminal projections do not preserve all higher-arity correlations.

failed_route_proposal.blocker: Only the auxiliary claim that three-pin projections determine full pentagon extendibility fails. C09 Section 3 gives a minimum four-pin counterexample and a separate full map of its source graph; the admitted route and root remain open.
